title: Laid work background
subtitle: Long parallel stitches that cover a shape entirely before a tying layer goes on top
excerpt: Laid work fills a shape with long parallel stitches that cover the ground fabric completely, then adds a second layer of stitches at right angles to tie and texture the surface.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), laid work entries.
heroPrompt: Laid work filling a leaf shape on linen, horizontal first-layer threads completely covering the ground, a second layer crossing diagonally, close-up, natural light.

content.text: Laid work covers the ground fabric with long stitches that go from one edge of the shape to the other without turning back on themselves. Unlike satin stitch, the stitches do not overlap; they sit side by side to cover the ground. A second layer of stitches then crosses the first at an angle and is tied down, adding texture and colour.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 3 strands for the first layer; 2 strands for the second layer

content.text: Start at the widest point. Bring the needle up on the left edge of the shape and insert on the right edge. The stitch lies straight across the full width.
Come up on the left edge just below the first stitch and cross to the right. Continue until the shape is covered.
Add the second layer at 45 degrees across the first, spacing stitches evenly.
At each intersection, add a small tying stitch to hold both layers flat.

items.symptom: Gaps appear between the first-layer stitches
items.fix: Keep each stitch immediately next to the previous one. They should touch but not overlap.

items.cause: Too much thread tension on long stitches.
items.fix: Keep the first layer at relaxed tension. The second layer and tying stitches will hold the shape flat.

content.text: Laid work is a core filling in Jacobean embroidery, where every leaf or petal is filled with a different laid pattern. It uses thread more efficiently than satin and is suitable for very large shapes where satin would be too heavy or costly.
